summary: Education-measurement researchers (DIPF) fit Many-Facet Rasch Models separately to human ratings (8 raters) and to ratings from 17 small open-weight LLM judges (0.8B-14B) on the 1,600 SummEval news summaries. They define 'residual hardness' (mean absolute post-fit residual) and show that moderate human-LLM agreement on latent summary quality (rho about 0.37) does not carry over to which summary-dimension units are hard to judge (rho about 0.09). Consistency is disproportionately LLM-hard, while coherence is human-hard.

claims.claim: Moderate alignment in latent quality does not imply alignment in residual hardness.
claims.evidence: §4.1: quality r=0.372 / rho=0.371 over 1,600 summaries. Residual hardness: summary level rho=0.176, summary-dimension level rho=0.089 over 6,400 units. Robust to the ≥7B-only panel (quality 0.408 vs hardness 0.039) and expert-only humans (0.688 vs 0.092). Fit diagnostics are in Table 1.

claims.claim: Mismatch is dimension-dependent: consistency shows an LLM-hard shift (+23.9 points), coherence a human-hard shift (-22.5).
claims.evidence: Table 2 under a median-split operational definition. The consistency gap persists (+26.2) in the expert vs ≥7B comparison; sensitivity checks are in App. A.2.5-A.2.6.

claims.claim: Human-easy/LLM-hard cases are partially predictable from observable source-summary features.
claims.evidence: Table 4: pooled AUROC 0.631, AUPRC 0.341 vs 23.3% base rate; relevance AUROC 0.717. Modest predictive power from class-balanced logistic regression with 5-fold CV. The authors frame the SHAP results as associations only.

patterns.note: Shows that the usual validation of LLM judges (score correlation with humans) hides case-level unreliability, especially on factual-consistency checks. But the judges are 0.8B-14B open models on news summarization, not frontier code reviewers.
Argues for routing predicted LLM-hard cases to human review; the predictor is only modestly accurate (AUROC 0.63).

methodology.sample: SummEval: 100 CNN/DailyMail sources x 16 systems = 1,600 summaries x 4 dimensions = 6,400 units; 8 human raters (3 expert, 5 crowd); 17 LLM judges.
methodology.baselines: Standard human-alignment correlations as the comparison point; psychometric fit diagnostics.
methodology.models: 17 open-weight judges, 0.8B-14B (Gemma, Qwen3.5, Phi, Llama, Mistral, OpenChat). No frontier or API judges.
methodology.variance: Greedy decoding (temperature 0), so no sampling variance. CIs are reported for the RQ3 predictors in the appendix. Multiple sensitivity analyses.
methodology.ablations: Judge-size subset, expert-only humans, rater misfit exclusion, calibration comparability, feature ablations, quadrant definitions.
methodology.contamination_controls: None. SummEval is public and may be in judges' pretraining data; not discussed.

standards.artifacts: Judge prompt and model list in App. A.1. No code or rating-data repository link found.

biases.detail: All judges are at most 14B open-weight models with only moderate quality alignment (rho about 0.37). The findings may not hold for frontier judges used in agent harnesses; the authors acknowledge 'stronger judge populations' as future work.
A single legacy news-summarization benchmark (SummEval); acknowledged in Limitations.
SummEval is old and public; possible exposure in judge pretraining is not discussed.

verdict_reason: off-topic: a psychometric analysis of small LLM judges on news-summary quality (SummEval). It is not about LLM agents, coding or software engineering. Methodologically careful (fit diagnostics, many sensitivity checks, peer-reviewed), but it does not inform harness decisions directly.
applicability: Does not transfer to the harness itself, which is Java services, multi-repo ingestion, mixed agent hosts and spec-driven development. One indirect cautionary point is worth keeping: if the team uses an LLM judge to grade ingested healthcare-education content or summaries before delivery, aggregate human agreement can hide case-level failures. Factual consistency against the source is the dimension where LLM judges diverge most, so source-grounding checks or human review should gate factual claims rather than an LLM score alone. The evidence comes from ≤14B judges on news summaries, so treat this as a hypothesis to test, not a measured property of frontier judges.
